Staff Software Engineer (AI Evals)

Contract | $100–$200/hour | 20-40 hrs/week | Start ASAP

We’re looking for highly experienced software engineer to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role.

You won’t be writing production code.
You’ll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What This Role Actually Is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios — focusing on:

  • Whether the response makes sense

  • Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

  • Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

  • Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste — not syntax correctness.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end-to-end

  • Judge whether outputs are:

    • Useful

    • Correct (at a high level)

    • Aligned with how a strong engineer would think

  • Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just code

  • Distinguish between different levels of response quality (e.g. what makes something a 2 vs 4)

  • Provide clear, opinionated feedback on:

    • What worked

    • What didn’t

    • What felt “off” or misleading

  • Help define what great looks like when interacting with tools like Cursor

What We Mean by “Taste”

We’re specifically looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

  • Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

  • Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

  • Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

  • Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments.

Who You Are

  • Staff / Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

  • Strong background in one of the below:

    • Go

    • Python

    • Rust

    • TypeScript / JavaScript

  • Hands-on experience using:

    • OpenAI Codex

    • Claude Code

    • Cursor

  • Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

  • Able to evaluate code without needing to fully execute or deeply review every line

  • Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

  • High bar for what “good engineering” looks like

Nice to Have

  • Experience with tools like Cursor or similar AI-first IDEs

  • Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

  • Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement Details

  • Rate: $100–$200/hour

  • Hours: ~20 hours+

  • Duration: Through October w/possible extentions

  • Start: ASAP

  • Process:

    • Take-home evaluation exercise

    • Background Check

    • Offer

Join the G2i Talent Pool

We’re always meeting great people in tech. Join the G2i Talent Pool and let us get to know you.

Who we’re looking for
Software, data, AI/ML, infrastructure, security, design, QA and product. Experienced or just starting out, fresh graduates are welcome. If you work in tech or are building your career in it, we’d love to meet you.

How it works

  1. Apply in a few minutes with your real details and links.

  2. We review your profile and send you a short technical assessment.

  3. Once you pass, you join our pool and hear from us when a project fits your skills.

Joining the pool doesn’t mean immediate work, since matching depends on what our clients need and on each profile. But we’re always working to match everyone in our pool with the right project.

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

DevOps Engineer — Mobile & Web (React Native / Expo)


Location: Fully remote — candidates worldwide
Engagement: Long-term contract

Budget: up to 46 USD per hour

About our Client

Our client is a software startup making sports training more engaging through gamification. Our platform connects training facilities, commercially available sensor systems, and players through mobile apps and the web, turning practice into a social and competitive experience.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on DevOps Engineer to own and improve our mobile and web build, release, and deployment workflows.

You’ll work with GitHub Actions, Expo, EAS, React Native, Supabase, Next.js, and React to help a small, fully remote engineering team ship reliable updates. Alongside release engineering, you’ll troubleshoot React Native issues, fix bugs, and contribute UI updates when needed.

What you’ll do

  • Manage, maintain, and optimize CI/CD pipelines, build systems, and deployment workflows for mobile and web applications.

  • Build and improve GitHub Actions workflows, including automated testing and release checks.

  • Manage iOS and Android builds and releases using Expo/EAS, App Store Connect, and Google Play Console.

  • Configure and manage over-the-air updates, versioning strategies, and release environments.

  • Support A/B testing frameworks and automated testing integrations.

  • Improve developer tooling, Supabase services, and infrastructure supporting Next.js and React applications.

  • Troubleshoot build and deployment failures and resolve React Native bugs and UI issues.

  • Take ownership of practical engineering tasks as priorities evolve.

What we’re looking for

  • 3+ years of experience in DevOps or infrastructure engineering focused on mobile and web platforms.

  • Strong hands-on experience with GitHub Actions, Expo, EAS, and React Native.

  • Proven experience managing production releases through both App Store Connect and Google Play Console.

  • Experience configuring versioning strategies, OTA updates, and A/B testing environments.

  • Proficiency with Supabase and the Next.js and React ecosystems.

  • Ability to make React Native code changes, including bug fixes and UI updates.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, ownership, and the ability to manage changing priorities in a small startup team.

Nice to have

  • Experience supporting automated end-to-end and integration tests in CI/CD.

  • Experience implementing 3D graphics in mobile applications outside gaming.

  • Experience developing for hardware sensors or integrating sensor data.

  • Meaningful engineering ownership of shipped cross-platform products.

  • Interest in product design, user experience, and software quality.

  • A love of baseball or other sports, particularly skills training.

Why join?

  • Work on a sports training platform connecting software with real-world practice.

  • Own mobile and web delivery workflows with a direct impact on the product and developer experience.

  • Join a small, fully remote team in a long-term contracting role.

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

Senior DevOps Engineer – FedRAMP

Location: East Coast, United States — Remote
Employment Type: Full-time
Annual Salary: $170,000–$200,000
Eligibility: U.S. citizenship required due to FedRAMP requirements

Big Ideas. Real People.

At our client, they believe that in the right environment and with the right team, talent has no boundaries. This team spirit, together with our drive to always aim high, has quickly earned us unicorn status and established Orca as a global cloud security innovation leader.

We’re looking for driven and talented people to join our mission to change the future of cloud security. If you’re ready to join a global team that inspires and challenges each other every day, now is the time to find your place in our pod.

Why our Client?

  • High growth: Over the past seven years, Orca has consistently achieved milestones that take other companies a decade or more. We have significantly expanded our team, customer reach, and product capabilities.

  • Disruptive innovation: Orca’s founders recognized that traditional security approaches were not built for the cloud. They pioneered agentless cloud security technology and continue to advance one of the industry’s most comprehensive cloud security platforms.

  • Well-capitalized: With a valuation of $1.8 billion, Orca is a cybersecurity unicorn backed by investors including CapitalG, ICONIQ, GGV, and SVCI.

  • Respectful and transparent culture: Our executives pride themselves on being accessible and openly sharing knowledge. Every employee has an opportunity to help shape the company and the future of cloud security.

About the Role

Our client is looking for a hands-on Senior DevOps Engineer to build, operate, monitor, and continuously improve the infrastructure supporting our U.S. federal and FedRAMP environments.

You will work with public-cloud infrastructure, production Kubernetes environments, infrastructure as code, CI/CD systems, observability, and security automation. You will also help ensure that Orca’s GovCloud and other relevant environments remain secure, reliable, scalable, and compliant.

This is one of a small number of U.S.-based engineering positions within a global R&D organization. You will work closely with engineering colleagues in Israel and serve as a key technical resource for Orca’s U.S. infrastructure.

The right candidate is a hands-on engineer who can build infrastructure from scratch, independently debug complex production incidents, make sound architectural decisions, and operate effectively in a fast-moving environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and implement solutions that improve new and existing cloud infrastructure.

  • Build, support, and operate infrastructure for FedRAMP-authorized environments.

  • Ensure the reliable and secure operation of Orca’s AWS GovCloud and other relevant environments.

  • Build, administer, and troubleshoot production Kubernetes environments.

  • Investigate Kubernetes and infrastructure incidents from initial symptoms through root-cause analysis and permanent remediation.

  • Develop reusable infrastructure-as-code components using Terraform.

  • Use Ansible to automate configuration, deployment, hardening, and operational processes.

  • Build and support development and production environments for Orca’s R&D organization.

  • Design and implement robust CI/CD pipelines.

  • Build monitoring, alerting, and self-healing capabilities.

  • Improve system observability through log analysis, dashboard development, and automated alerts based on established SLOs and SLAs.

  • Apply continuous dependency upgrades and remediate vulnerabilities within FedRAMP environments.

  • Assess infrastructure and deployment procedures to ensure compliance with internal policies and external regulations.

  • Respond to system and production issues in a timely manner.

  • Collaborate with engineering, security, and compliance teams when FedRAMP requirements affect infrastructure or operational decisions.

  • Follow Orca’s policies and procedures related to internal privileged-access rights.

  • Participate in regular collaboration with Orca’s Israel-based engineering team, including an 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time standup Monday through Thursday.

Who You Are

  • You are a U.S. citizen, as required for this FedRAMP environment.

  • You are based on the U.S. East Coast or can consistently work an East Coast schedule.

  • You have at least three years of experience in DevOps, infrastructure, platform, cloud, or site reliability engineering.

  • You have at least two to three years of meaningful, hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production.

  • You have personally built or substantially designed cloud infrastructure using Terraform or comparable infrastructure-as-code tooling.

  • You understand Terraform modules, state management, environment separation, code review, and CI/CD practices.

  • You have practical experience with Ansible for configuration management and automation.

  • You have experience building, operating, or directly supporting infrastructure within a FedRAMP-authorized environment.

  • You have strong experience working with public-cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS and AWS GovCloud.

  • You have designed and implemented sophisticated CI/CD pipelines.

  • You have experience with monitoring and observability tools such as Prometheus, Graphite, Grafana, CloudWatch, or similar platforms.

  • You have hands-on experience with Kubernetes and Helm.

  • You have programming experience with Python, Java, or Go, along with scripting experience using Bash or a similar language.

  • You understand system-level concepts including operating systems, networking, storage, and file-system management.

  • You can diagnose production problems independently and communicate the root cause, remediation, and preventive actions clearly.

  • You are self-driven, resourceful, organized, and eager to learn.

  • You have strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

  • You have excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • You hold a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

FedRAMP Experience

The strongest candidates will have directly participated in a FedRAMP authorization or continuous monitoring program, with experience in areas such as:

  • Operating AWS GovCloud infrastructure.

  • Implementing or maintaining security controls.

  • Defining or supporting authorization boundaries.

  • Resolving POA&M items.

  • Collecting technical evidence for audits.

  • Managing continuous monitoring and vulnerability remediation.

  • Working within FIPS requirements.

  • Supporting recurring audits or working with compliance teams and external assessors.

Candidates may still qualify if they worked hands-on as a DevOps, platform, cloud, or infrastructure engineer within a FedRAMP-compliant organization, even if they did not personally lead the entire authorization process.

General knowledge of FedRAMP without practical engineering involvement will not be sufficient.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and equity package.

  • Discounted medical, dental, and vision benefits with significant employer contributions.

  • Benefits coverage beginning on your first day of employment.

  • Generous paid time off with U.S. holidays observed.

  • Flexible remote work environment.

  • Your choice of a Mac or Windows laptop.

  • Work-from-home stipend during your first month of employment.

  • Monthly reimbursement for your cell phone and home internet.

  • The opportunity to collaborate with talented colleagues around the world.

The annual salary range for this position is $170,000–$200,000. This represents the typical range based on experience, skills, and other relevant factors.

This position is open until filled. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis.

Our client is an equal-opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected

veteran status, disability status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Head of Psysical AI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Head of Physical AI

Location: Remote — Europe and the United States preferred; exceptional candidates globally will be considered
Employment: Full-time
Reports to: CEO
Role type: Hands-on technical leader and team builder
Travel: As needed

About our Client

Our client builds the data, evaluation, and deployment layer for Physical AI.

The company works across multimodal robot and human data, annotation and assurance, model evaluation, and the systems that turn physical-world experience into useful robot behavior.

Miraxis is hardware- and model-agnostic. What matters is whether a dataset, model, or method produces a measurable improvement on a real task. The company will build focused model and evaluation capabilities where they strengthen its data products, demonstrate the value of its data, or solve a clear customer or partner problem.

The role

Our client is looking for a Head of Physical AI to establish and lead its AI research and engineering function.

You will decide which Physical AI problems the company pursues, define how results are evaluated, and remain directly involved in the most important technical work. You will connect four areas that are often treated separately:

  • Multimodal and embodied data

  • Transformer-based models and robot policies

  • Rigorous offline and real-world evaluation

  • Deployment on physical systems

This is a player-coach role. During your first year, at least half of your time will be spent on direct technical work: designing models and experiments, writing or reviewing code, inspecting data, debugging training runs, analyzing failures, and reviewing robot rollouts.

You will also build a small, focused team of researchers and engineers as the work requires it.

What you’ll do

  • Define a focused Physical AI research and engineering roadmap with clear hypotheses, baselines, milestones, success measures, and stop criteria.

  • Select the model families Miraxis should train, adapt, or evaluate and determine when to build internally, use open models, license technology, or work through partners.

  • Personally design, adapt, train, and evaluate Transformer-based systems for embodied tasks.

  • Work across areas such as vision-language-action models, multimodal Transformers, robot foundation models, action representation, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, world models, cross-embodiment transfer, and robot-policy evaluation.

  • Define the sensors, modalities, annotations, data mixtures, coverage, and quality controls required to train and evaluate selected models.

  • Measure how data quality, diversity, and composition affect model behavior and real-world task performance.

  • Establish reproducible offline and real-world evaluation systems, baselines, held-out conditions, and release gates.

  • Protect evaluations against leakage, overfitting, and weak or misleading success criteria.

  • Take projects from problem definition through training, hardware integration, and real-world validation.

  • Analyze failures across data, perception, models, control, hardware, and the operating environment.

  • Design safe, staged physical testing and deployment plans with clear supervision and rollback mechanisms.

  • Recruit and lead a small team of complementary researchers and engineers.

  • Lead architecture, experiment, code, rollout, and failure reviews.

  • Translate customer and partner needs into testable technical requirements.

  • Communicate technical strategy, evidence, uncertainty, and limitations clearly to customers, partners, and investors.

What we’re looking for

Deep, hands-on Transformer expertise

This is a hard requirement. You must have personally made material architecture or training decisions in at least one substantial Transformer-based system, such as:

  • Vision Transformers

  • Vision-language or vision-language-action models

  • Multimodal foundation models

  • Decision Transformers

  • Diffusion Transformers

  • Video Transformers

  • World models

  • Transformer-based perception, planning, or control systems

You should be able to explain how you represented and tokenized inputs and outputs, fused modalities, structured attention and temporal context, selected losses, built data mixtures, distributed and monitored training, diagnosed failures, and changed the system to improve task performance.

Using hosted model APIs, prompting language models, or running an unchanged public training recipe does not meet this requirement.

Physical AI experience

You have worked on machine learning for a system that perceives or acts in the physical world, such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, industrial automation, manipulation, mobile robots, humanoids, or wearable and egocentric systems.

At least one substantial project must have progressed beyond offline datasets or simulation into a real or operational physical system. Simulation experience qualifies only when paired with credible sim-to-real ownership and physical validation.

Hands-on technical ability

  • Strong Python engineering skills

  • Direct experience with PyTorch or an equivalent deep-learning framework

  • Ability to read and debug unfamiliar model and training code

  • Experience designing controlled experiments and analyzing rollout failures

  • Experience working with large multimodal datasets

  • Sound judgment around compute, memory, training stability, inference latency, and cost

Technical leadership

You have set the direction for a significant research, model-development, robotics, or cross-functional technical program. You have made architecture and resource decisions, mentored or hired technical talent, stopped weak lines of work, and helped take a result into deployment.

A management title is not required, but direct technical ownership is.

Strongly preferred

Candidates combining deep Transformer expertise with strong computer-vision experience will receive priority. Relevant areas include:

  • Visual representation learning

  • VLMs and video or temporal modeling

  • Detection, segmentation, and tracking

  • Multi-view and egocentric vision

  • 3D and spatial reasoning

  • Pose estimation, calibration, and localization

  • Sensor fusion

  • Real-time vision systems

Additional valuable experience includes:

  • Vision-language-action models or robot foundation models

  • Action tokenization or continuous action generation

  • Diffusion or flow-matching policies

  • Imitation learning or reinforcement learning

  • World models and cross-embodiment training

  • Robot manipulation

  • Distributed training and inference optimization

  • ROS 2

  • Sim-to-real transfer

  • Safety-critical systems

  • Widely used open-source work or personally owned research publications

  • Early-stage company experience

  • Work with technical customers or research partners

A PhD in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, computer science, or a related field is valuable but not required. An equivalent record of original model work, technical leadership, and real-system delivery is equally relevant.

Miraxis cares most about what you personally designed, trained, evaluated, and deployed.

What success looks like

Within 90 days:

  • Audit Miraxis’s data, evaluation assets, partnerships, and model opportunities.

  • Select one or two focused research bets.

  • Establish a reproducible model baseline and initial evaluation suite.

  • Define a credible path to physical validation.

  • Present a practical 12-month roadmap supported by working technical evidence.

Within six months:

  • Train, adapt, or rigorously evaluate at least one relevant Transformer-based model or robot policy.

  • Confirm or reject at least one important technical hypothesis.

  • Establish a repeatable data-to-training-to-evaluation workflow.

  • Test on a real robot, directly or through a credible hardware partner.

  • Document representative failures and their implications.

Within twelve months:

  • Demonstrate a measurable improvement attributable to Miraxis data, methods, or assurance systems.

  • Close the loop between model failures, data decisions, retraining, and re-evaluation.

  • Deliver a model, benchmark, evaluation system, or deployment that a customer or partner can use.

  • Build a small team capable of running the work without unnecessary process layers.

Success will be judged by decision quality, reproducibility, real-system results, and customer value—not by team size, paper count, parameter count, or experiment volume.

 - Recruit and lead a small team of complementary researchers and engineers.

 - Lead architecture, experiment, code, rollout, and failure reviews.

 - Translate customer and partner needs into testable technical requirements.

DEEP, HANDS-ON TRANSFORMER EXPERTISE

 - Vision Transformers

 - Vision-language or vision-language-action models

 - Multimodal foundation models

 - Decision Transformers

 - Diffusion Transformers

 - Video Transformers

 - World models

 - Transformer-based perception, planning, or control systems

You should be able to explain how you represented and tokenized inputs and outputs, fused modalities, structured attention and temporal context, selected losses, built data mixtures, distributed and monitored training, diagnosed failures, and changed the system to improve task performance.

Using hosted model APIs, prompting language models, or running an unchanged public training recipe does not meet this requirement.


PHYSICAL AI EXPERIENCE

You have worked on machine learning for a system that perceives or acts in the physical world, such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, industrial automation, manipulation, mobile robots, humanoids, or wearable and egocentric systems.

 - Strong Python engineering skills

 - Direct experience with PyTorch or an equivalent deep-learning framework

 - Ability to read and debug unfamiliar model and training code

 - Experience designing controlled experiments and analyzing rollout failures

 - Experience working with large multimodal datasets

 - Sound judgment around compute, memory, training stability, inference latency, and cost

 - Visual representation learning

 - VLMs and video or temporal modeling

 - Detection, segmentation, and tracking

 - Multi-view and egocentric vision

 - 3D and spatial reasoning

 - Pose estimation, calibration, and localization

 - Sensor fusion

 - Vision-language-action models or robot foundation models

 - Action tokenization or continuous action generation

 - Diffusion or flow-matching policies

 - Imitation learning or reinforcement learning

 - World models and cross-embodiment training

 - Robot manipulation

 - Work with technical customers or research partners

 - Audit Miraxis’s data, evaluation assets, partnerships, and model opportunities.

 - Select one or two focused research bets.

 - Establish a reproducible model baseline and initial evaluation suite.

 - Define a credible path to physical validation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

Check out this Loom video for more details: https://www.loom.com/share/b0d1b0bf24c44ae8b95dca84b9db60e5

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What this role actually is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

• Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

• Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

• Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.

What you'll be doing

• Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end

• Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think

• Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code

• Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)

• Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading

• Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

• Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

• Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

• Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

• Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.

Who you are

• Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

• Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python

• Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor

• Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

• Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line

• Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement

• Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

• High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

• Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

• Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

• Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well

• Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat

• Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Senior Product Manager, Data & AI (Document Intelligence)
· Remote (continental US, Eastern Time) · DC/Metro area preferred
Fulltime role

About this opportunity
G2i is hiring on behalf of one of our clients, a fast-growing, DC-based government services firm. Since 2009 they have helped federal agencies and large government primes in three areas: research and data analysis, advanced data science, and strategic services. They currently support several analytics and research programs across HHS. The team is collaborative and small enough that your work is visible, and they take work-life balance seriously.


The role
You'll own the product roadmap for the client's document intelligence platform. You'll turn customer and reviewer needs into clear, testable requirements and make sure each problem is fixed in the right place. That could be the UX, the source data, the extraction pipeline, the model, the search logic, the thresholds, or the business rules.

This role suits a product leader who knows that AI products need measurable definitions of quality: accuracy, false-positive rates, reviewer effort, evidence requirements and operational performance.


What you'll do

  • Own the roadmap and priorities across data engineering, data science, backend, search and frontend teams

  • Lead discovery with clients and internal stakeholders using prototypes, demos and working software

  • Turn business needs into requirements, user stories, business rules and measurable acceptance criteria

  • Define requirements for document processing, alerts, scoring, evidence presentation, search, review workflows and source traceability

  • Work with data scientists on evaluation datasets, model metrics, confidence thresholds, and acceptable false-positive and false-negative rates

  • Work with data engineers on ingestion, normalization, metadata, lineage, processing completeness and data quality

  • Diagnose whether an issue comes from the UI, data, model, pipeline, search, thresholds or business rules

  • Favor reusable platform capabilities over one-off client customizations

  • Coordinate release readiness, client demos and structured feedback

  • Measure accuracy, completeness, reviewer effort, latency, reliability, adoption and cost

  • Communicate priorities, tradeoffs and limitations clearly to clients and internal teams


What you bring

  • Senior PM experience delivering AI/ML, data-intensive, search or workflow products

  • Experience prioritizing work across data, ML, backend and frontend teams

  • A track record of discovery driven by prototypes or demos

  • Skill turning business needs into detailed, technical, testable requirements

  • Experience defining acceptance criteria for probabilistic features such as model outputs, alerts, recommendations or rankings

  • A solid grasp of data pipelines, APIs, data quality, system dependencies and model behavior

  • Close working experience with data scientists, data engineers, software engineers and UX

  • Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, writing and decision-making


Requirements

  • Authorized to work in the US, with 3+ consecutive years living in the US

  • Able and willing to obtain a Public Trust clearance


Nice to have

  • Document intelligence, OCR, semantic or vector search, generative AI, or human-in-the-loop workflows

  • Products built on AWS (e.g. S3, DynamoDB, OpenSearch, Step Functions, SQS, EventBridge, Bedrock, SageMaker, Textract)

  • Regulated, healthcare, medical-device or other high-stakes products

  • Model governance, explainability, evidence traceability and reviewer workflows

  • Supporting multiple clients while keeping one coherent, reusable roadmap

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Senior Full Stack Developer — Web3

Remote — International | Full-time

Salary - up to 90k USD

About the opportunity

G2i is recruiting a Senior Full Stack Developer for Moonberg, a Zug-based intelligence lab building proprietary market intelligence and infrastructure for decentralized markets.

Moonberg processes more than 700 real-time data streams, from on-chain activity to market narratives, to generate actionable insights. Its consumer product, Obzidian, is an agentic trading terminal designed to research, monitor, and execute across markets around the clock.

We’re looking for a highly experienced engineer who can own architecture and implementation across frontend, backend, and Web3 integrations. You should be comfortable scaling data-intensive systems, solving production problems, and making technical decisions with substantial autonomy.

What you’ll do

  • Own full stack development across React interfaces, Node.js services, and Web3 integrations.

  • Build and scale decentralized applications integrating wallets, DeFi protocols, and on-chain data.

  • Integrate Web3 libraries, SDKs, packages, and APIs into reliable product workflows.

  • Design systems for performance, security, scalability, and interoperability.

  • Build and improve infrastructure supporting large volumes of real-time market and blockchain data.

  • Investigate production issues and improve system reliability.

  • Collaborate with experienced engineers on architecture and research into emerging technologies.

  • Take features from technical design through implementation, deployment, and production support.

What you’ll bring

  • 10+ years of professional software development experience.

  • At least 3 years of full stack development experience with a strong Web3 focus.

  • Strong proficiency in TypeScript, React, and Node.js.

  • Hands-on experience shipping Web3 applications or integrations into production.

  • Experience integrating wallets, DeFi services, on-chain data, and third-party Web3 packages or APIs.

  • Experience designing and scaling data-intensive systems.

  • Strong architectural judgment and a practical approach to performance, security, and reliability.

  • Fluent English.

  • The ability to work independently, communicate clearly, and take ownership in a fast-moving startup.

Nice to have

  • Multi-chain development experience, ideally across both Ethereum and Solana.

  • Experience with Prisma, Zod, tRPC, and Fastify.

Working at Moonberg

Moonberg operates with a fully senior team, few meetings, and a direct, execution-focused culture. Engineers have substantial ownership and are expected to move quickly while maintaining high technical standards.

The pace is demanding, and this is not a conventional 9-to-5 environment. The role suits someone comfortable with startup intensity, broad responsibility, and accountability for production outcomes.

What’s offered

  • Fully remote work with flexible hours.

  • Competitive compensation based on experience.

  • Collaboration with highly experienced engineers.

  • Significant technical ownership and autonomy.

  • The opportunity to build core infrastructure and products in the Web3 space.

How to apply

Apply through G2i with your resume and links to your GitHub, portfolio, or relevant projects. Please highlight your production Web3 experience and your contributions across frontend, backend, and blockchain integrations.

jobs.title: Remote Senior Software Engineer, (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

Check out this Loom video for more details: https://www.loom.com/share/b0d1b0bf24c44ae8b95dca84b9db60e5

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What this role actually is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

• Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

• Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

• Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.

What you'll be doing

• Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end

• Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think

• Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code

• Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)

• Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading

• Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

• Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

• Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

• Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

• Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.

Who you are

• Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

• Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python

• Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor

• Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

• Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line

• Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement

• Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

• High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

• Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

• Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

• Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well

• Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat

• Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview
